title: 123tutors
body:
The project

123tutors matches students with tutors. The platform had outgrown the no-code foundation it launched on, and at the same time students needed more support than a tutor roster alone could provide, help at 11pm the night before an exam, when no tutor is online.

I returned as CTO to solve both at once: move the platform onto a foundation it could grow on, and give students an AI tutor that is always available.

What I did

  • Led a full platform migration from Bubble to Next.js/TypeScript on Prisma and Supabase, without losing the existing user base or data.
  • Shipped a Claude-powered AI Tutor via AWS Bedrock, with real-time streaming chat and intent classification.
  • Built generated interactive mindmaps so the AI Tutor can lay a concept out visually, not just in text.
  • Set the technical roadmap now extending into the platform''s matching engine and institutional reporting.

Where it landed

Migration live, AI Tutor shipped and in daily use by students. The platform now runs on a stack the team can extend, instead of one they had to work around.

title: Akur8 UAT Runner
body:
The project

Alpha Insure prices motor insurance through Akur8, a third-party actuarial rating engine. Before any pricing change reaches a real customer quote, it has to be validated against hundreds of scenarios, and doing that by hand, one case at a time, was slow, error-prone, and didn''t scale with how often the rating logic changed.

This tool exists to make that validation fast, repeatable, and auditable.

What I did

  • Built the full stack solo, React/Vite frontend, Node/Express backend, and Firebase/Firestore for storage and history, end to end.
  • Bulk test execution, upload CSV-defined test batches that run sequentially against the Akur8 rating API, with live pass/fail/error tracking as the run progresses.
  • Input validation up front, invalid rows are flagged before a run starts, so a malformed test case never silently burns a batch.
  • Auditable history, every run is stored and searchable in Firestore, and results export cleanly for re-import and comparison.

Where it landed

The tool is in active use for pre-deploy validation of Alpha Insure''s motor pricing. What used to be a manual, one-at-a-time check is now a bulk run with a clear pass/fail signal and a full audit trail, the kind of safety net that lets a pricing team ship changes with confidence.
desc: Akur8 UAT Runner: a full-stack tool for bulk-validating an actuarial motor rating API. Built by Rusumba Bukanga with React, Vite, Node/Express and Firebase.

title: The Operations Layer
body:
The project

Three very different businesses, insurance, hospitality, fitness, each running on manual processes that did not scale: paper-heavy underwriting, phone-in reservations, and monthly billing done by hand.

The work was to replace those manual processes with systems, across all four businesses, alongside the Alpha engineering team.

What I did

  • Insurance: CRM systems for underwriting, claims, and broker management; customer-facing quote calculators and policy portals; a broker onboarding workflow; and REST APIs integrating underwriting partners, banks, and reinsurers.
  • Hospitality: a real-time booking and capacity-management system for a high-traffic rooftop restaurant.
  • Fitness: a membership platform plus an automated recurring debit-order run, scheduled batch billing with bank reconciliation, on Lambda, EventBridge, S3, and SES/SNS.
  • Internal: an HR portal with org-chart, employee self-service, and a wellness booking system, integrated with Microsoft Graph.

Where it landed

All in production. Policy processing time is down 60% and manual data-entry errors down 85%, the measurable result of turning manual workflows into systems.

title: SSO Authentication Gateway
body:
The project

One organisation, three completely different businesses under it: an insurance operation, a restaurant, and a gym. Each had its own applications, its own users, and its own login, but all of it had to be centrally managed, secure, and consistent.

The answer was a single authentication gateway every application could sit behind, rather than each one reinventing login on its own.

What I did

  • Architected the gateway and worked with the Alpha engineering team to build it, a centralised auth service every application in the ecosystem authenticates through.
  • Built on AWS Cognito with KMS-signed JWTs, so session tokens are verifiable and tamper-evident across services.
  • Implemented an OAuth2/PKCE flow on Lambda and API Gateway, with DynamoDB backing identity and session state.
  • Collaborated across the team on rollout to underwriting, client-facing, and internal HR systems without disrupting existing users.

Where it landed

In production, underpinning underwriting, client-facing, and internal HR systems across the group. One login layer instead of many, centrally managed, and secure by design.

title: Claim Forms Modernisation
body:
The project

Hundreds of claims forms were trapped in a deprecated, Adobe-only PDF format. A customer on Chrome, Safari, or a phone hit a dead end, they had to install desktop software just to file a claim. In an insurance context, that is lost claims and frustrated customers.

The job was to free those forms from Adobe entirely, and to replace a paid third-party signing tool while we were at it.

What I did

  • Helped architect an in-browser pipeline, with the Alpha engineering team, that reads each form''s own underlying blueprint and reconstructs it as a fully interactive web form.
  • Preserved conditional logic, calculations, and draw-to-sign, then exported a pixel-accurate PDF on submission, identical to the original on paper.
  • Built an in-house document execution and e-signature platform that replaced a paid third-party subscription entirely.
  • Rolled it out across the full form library, working end-to-end from browse to signed, submitted PDF.

Where it landed

Rolled out across the full form library, working end-to-end from any browser to a signed, submitted PDF. The e-signature platform is live handling agreement workflows, and the Adobe dependency is gone.

title: Cleverly AI
body:
The project

Manual grading does not scale for South African schools, colleges, and universities. But the obvious fix, AI that grades for you, runs into a harder problem: a teacher will not trust a mark they cannot see the reasoning behind.

Cleverly is built around that tension. The goal was never to replace the teacher, but to do the heavy lifting and then show its work.

What I did

  • Founded the company and set the technical direction as Cofounder & CTO, owning architecture, AI systems, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Built a vendor-neutral AI provider layer so the grading engine is not locked to a single LLM, models can be swapped or tiered by cost and task.
  • Designed evidence-linked, rubric-aligned grading with a teacher-in-the-loop review step, so every mark traces back to the rubric and the student''s own work.
  • Built a tiered OCR pipeline that balances cost against handwriting-recognition accuracy, routing harder scripts to stronger models only when needed.

Where it landed

Live in pilot with South African educational institutions. Prompt caching and model tiering keep the unit economics sustainable as usage scales, the difference between a demo and a business.

title: Friends of Cinema
body:
The project

An independent film production company needed a website that felt like the films they make, art-house, editorial, cinematic, not another templated agency homepage. For a creative studio, the site is a portfolio piece in its own right.

I built it solo, front to back, with the visual craft the brief demanded.

What I did

  • Built the full React/Vite/TypeScript site end to end, solo.
  • Crafted the motion and feel, Framer Motion page transitions, a custom cursor with mix-blend-mode effects, and a full-screen parallax hero with a film-grain overlay.
  • Built a filterable portfolio grid for their film work.
  • Backed it with Supabase (Postgres, Storage, Auth) on a client-manageable content schema with RLS policies, so the studio can update it themselves.

Where it landed

Live in production on Vercel, a site that carries the studio''s creative identity rather than flattening it into a template.

title: Property Portfolio Rebuild
body:
The project

A property development company''s public site was running on a five-year-old template-based stack. Every content update was a risk, and the underlying framework was long past its supportable life, the kind of technical debt that quietly gets more expensive every month.

The work was a full rebuild that modernised the foundation without changing what the public and existing clients already relied on.

What I did

  • Helped architect a full rebuild, with the team, onto a modern Next.js architecture.
  • Migrated every property listing, gallery, and page into structured, maintainable data models.
  • Preserved exact public-facing content and behaviour, so nothing clients depended on shifted underneath them.
  • Verified page-by-page against the live site for full content and visual parity ahead of cutover.

Where it landed

In final QA, verified page-by-page against the live production site for full content and visual parity ahead of cutover, a modern, maintainable foundation replacing an unsupportable one.

title: Tutor Vetting Automation
body:
The project

Every tutor application was manually reviewed by an admin before going live, a human bottleneck that could not scale past roughly 50 applications a week, with no verifiable identity or background checks behind it. For a platform putting tutors in front of students, that is both a growth ceiling and a trust problem.

The work was to automate vetting end to end, without lowering the bar on who gets approved.

What I did

  • Built an automated vetting pipeline integrating a South African identity verification API (InTouch).
  • Wired in government ID verification, facial-match and liveness biometrics, AML/sanctions screening, and bank-account verification, running in parallel.
  • Built a tiered decision engine that auto-approves clean applications and flags edge cases for human review.
  • Cut the admin out of the happy path, leaving humans to handle only genuine exceptions.

Where it landed

Vetting time dropped from 2–5 business days to under 2 hours. Admin time per application fell from ~30 minutes to ~2 minutes on the review queue only, and the scalability ceiling is gone entirely.

title: uTap
body:
The project

University campuses run on cash and cards that vendors cannot always process, and students already carry a physical ID card that does nothing beyond proving who they are. uTap turns that card into a payment method and the phone into the terminal.

I joined as an engineer with equity in the venture, owning core technical pieces of the build.

What I did

  • Worked across a multi-app ecosystem: a React Native/Expo student app, a vendor dashboard, and an admin portal.
  • Led the full payment gateway migration onto Paystack across mobile, web, and backend.
  • Contributed to the NFC tap-to-pay work, the piece that lets a student tap to pay with their student card.
  • Took iOS NFC as far as the platform currently allows, with support in progress pending permissions.

Where it landed

Preparing for pilot launch with an initial university partner, with iOS NFC support in progress. The student app, vendor dashboard, and admin portal are built and integrated on Paystack.
